endorsements.quote: This iterative approach, supported by ongoing monitoring, would ensure that the NICE ESF remains adaptive to the pace of technological development.
Structured workshops and pilot programs can help embed these technologies in real-world settings, fostering trust and usability [ 21 ].

unlisted_practices: Transition the NICE evidence standards framework from a static framework to a dynamic, adaptive model with a bidirectional feedback mechanism in which real-world evidence informs regular updates.
Introduce modular evaluation processes that assess different aspects of digital health technologies as they evolve, updating efficacy and safety assessments as real-world data accumulate.
Establish a regulatory sandbox for testing digital health technologies in controlled real-world settings with iterative refinement based on feedback.
Develop shared repositories of anonymized health data with collaborative data governance to support training of machine learning models.
Co-design real-world evidence generation strategies with industry partners.
Embed privacy-by-design principles, including data anonymization, encryption, and user-controlled data sharing, in the development life cycle of digital health tools.
Use federated learning and adaptive trial designs to evaluate AI algorithms without compromising data privacy.
Systematically engage stakeholders through interviews, focus groups, Delphi panels, and workshops in regulatory and adoption processes.
Provide government funding, regulatory flexibility, and infrastructure support to small-to-medium enterprises and start-ups developing digital health technologies.
Provide training programs and continuous professional development to equip staff to use new digital technologies.

screen.reason: This is a framework and policy commentary evaluating the NICE Evidence Standards Framework for digital health technologies and proposing recommendations for dynamic, real-world evidence-based evaluation of evolving AI technologies.
